source_text: Postea quoque ad legem ventum est, ad cuius usque tempus perscripsit Apostolus non ostensum viguisse peccatum; quod tu tempus usque ad finem legis protelare conatus es non intellegens nequidquam te argumentatum, quandoquidem constringendus a nobis esses, ut probares hoc peccatum, de quo mentiris Paulum locutum et quod asseris usque ad abolitionem regnasse Veteris Testamenti, vel imputatum fuisse vel imputari potuisse sub lege, vel certe acquiesceres non regnare post Christum, ut sensibus tuis saltem inflexa violenter Apostoli sententia consonaret. Horum autem nihil reddi a te potest; fidei ergo nostrae in solido est puritas collocata, cui et rationis instituta et iustitiae dignitas et Apostoli per omnia scita conveniunt.
pass_a_gloss: Afterward also it was come to the law, until whose time the Apostle wrote that sin not shown flourished; which time you tried to stretch even to the end of the law, not understanding that you had argued in vain, seeing that you would have to be constrained by us, so that you would prove this sin, about which you lie that Paul spoke and which you assert reigned even to the abolition of the Old Testament, either was imputed or could have been imputed under the law, or certainly you would acquiesce that it does not reign after Christ, so that at least the Apostle's sentence, violently bent, would sound together with your senses. But none of these things can be rendered by you; the purity of our faith therefore has been placed on the solid, with which both the institutes of reason and the dignity of justice and the Apostle's decrees through all things agree.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Afterward we came to the law. The apostle wrote that undisclosed sin prevailed until its time (Romans 5:13). You tried to extend that time until the law’s end, without understanding that your argument was futile. For we would compel you either to prove that this sin—which you falsely claim Paul discussed, and which you assert reigned until the Old Testament was abolished—was or could have been imputed under the law; or else to agree that it does not reign after Christ. At least then the apostle’s statement, though violently twisted, would agree with your views. But you can deliver none of this. The purity of our faith therefore stands on solid ground, in agreement with reason’s principles, justice’s dignity, and all the apostle’s teachings.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)
